org: Visma (Visma Unified Design, VUD Product Design System)
accessNotes: VUD is a Supernova-hosted site; prose is minimal and most best-practice guidance is conveyed through do/don't SVG illustrations (downloaded, rasterised with ImageMagick and inspected). The Specifications page HTML lists all chart tokens with light/dark values; the @vismaux/vud npm package token CSS was used to confirm the categorical sequence and fonts. No explicit rules on titles, source lines, number formats or axis styling exist; structure notes are inferred from the guide's illustrations.
summary: Enterprise SaaS product-UI chart guidance (finance, HR, payroll software). Charts are clean and light: thin light-grey horizontal gridlines, no axis lines except a baseline, small grey tick text, rotated y-axis title, and a bottom-centred legend with round swatches. Colour comes from colour-blind-safe ColorBrewer-derived token schemes (brown/orange/pink/purple/teal/green/blue) with explicit light and dark-mode values, a single brand blue #116fae for one-colour charts, and grey for less important data. Best practices: limit colours, use shapes/line styles for accessibility, and give hover feedback by dimming non-focused marks with a value tooltip.

colors.categoricalNotes: Categorical tokens scheme-a..scheme-e-categorical-chart: brown-50 #8c510a, orange-50 #d73027, purple-30 #a06fae, teal-40 #2b8078, blue-40 #638ec2 (light mode). Note 'Follow the numbered sequence.' Dark mode values: #f6e8c3, #fee090, #b791c2, #9ad0ca (+ blue lighter). Specifications page shows schemes a-d; npm tokens add scheme-e. For a single series use chart-brand #116fae; use chart-neutral #dadada for less important data points. Best practice: limit the number of colours (one colour for one measure rather than a rainbow).
colors.notes: Chart UI tokens (light / dark): chart-text-default #252626 / #c3d0d9 (labels); chart-text-secondary #494a4a / #c3d0d9 (legends); chart-text-inverse #ffffff / #000000 (text on chart colours, only if needed); chart-border #8a8a8a / #9aa5ae (gridlines); chart-brand #116fae / #116fae; chart-neutral #dadada / #6f7a82; chart surface #ffffff / #2b3033. Seven 6-step sequential schemes, each with a border token: a brown #f6e8c3 #e5c891 #d0a969 #ba8b47 #a36e29 #8c510a; b orange #fee090 #febf79 #f99e63 #f17c4d #e5593a #d73027; c pink #fde0ef #f3bed9 #e99cc2 #de78ab #d25294 #c51b7d; d purple #e7d4e8 #ceb2d6 #b791c2 #a06fae #8b4e99 #762a83; e teal #c7eae5 #9ad0ca #72b6ae #4d9b93 #2b8078 #01665e; f green #e6f5d0 #c3e39e #a2d077 #84bb56 #68a73a #4d9221; g blue (listed above). Dark mode reverses each ramp. Four 6-step diverging schemes: a brown-teal, b pink-green, c orange-blue (listed above), d purple-green, each with chart-border-start/end tokens. Every fill scheme has a darker 'chart-border' stroke token (e.g. brown #a36e29). Single-colour palette 'represents your brand's visual language' (progress bars). All tokens described as colour-blind safe.

axisTitle.placement: rotated, left of the y axis (e.g. 'Rainfall (mm)')

dataLabel.weight: bold for the main value in tooltips

typography.notes: VUD body font is Open Sans (--font-family-base), headings Ubuntu (--font-family-primary). Chart labels use chart-text-default; legends use chart-text-secondary. No chart-specific sizes published.

structure.gridlines: Horizontal only (for vertical charts), thin, light grey (token chart-border #8a8a8a for gridlines; illustrations render them very light).
structure.axisLine: No y-axis line; thin baseline at the bottom of the plot only (illustrations).
structure.zeroLine: Baseline at 0 coincides with bottom gridline.
structure.yAxisTitle: rotated 90 degrees, left of tick labels, with unit in parentheses
structure.unitPlacement: in axis title in parentheses, e.g. 'Rainfall (mm)', 'Price U.S. Dollars'
structure.frame: none in the chart; sits on chart surface token (#ffffff light / #2b3033 dark)
structure.notes: Horizontal bar example shows category labels left and value axis at bottom with no gridlines.

marks.bars: Medium-width bars with clear gaps; horizontal bars have slightly rounded ends in illustrations; stacked segments separated by a thin white gap/line.
marks.lines: Use different shapes (markers), line styles and thicknesses to distinguish series for accessibility.
marks.pies: Allowed - pie chart shown as example of the categorical palette.
marks.notes: Fills may be stroked with the scheme's darker chart-border token.

labels.dataLabels: Not printed by default; values appear in hover tooltip (large bold value e.g. '38%' with secondary line '15 tasks').

furniture.other: Charts embedded in product UI; progress bars use the single-colour brand palette.

interaction: Provide better visual feedback: on hover, the hovered segment/bar keeps its colour while the other bars are dimmed (rendered darker/muted), and a tooltip-like value callout appears near the cursor with a bold value ('38%') and a regular sub-line ('15 tasks'). Hover surface token chart-hover = list-surface-hover. Full dark-mode token set.
accessibility: All palettes are colour-blind safe ('View colourblind helper' per scheme); avoid red/green pairings (the 'don't' uses green+blue similar lightness; the 'do' uses pink+light green with distinct lightness); on line charts use different shapes, lines and thicknesses; chart-text-inverse only when needed on coloured fills.

chartTypes.notes: Rainbow colouring of a single-measure bar chart is a documented 'don't'.

distinctiveRules.rule: A single-measure chart uses one colour (brand blue #116fae), never one colour per bar.
distinctiveRules.quote: Limit the number of colours (do: all bars blue; don't: rainbow bars)

distinctiveRules.rule: chart-brand #116fae is the primary chart colour when only one colour is required; chart-neutral #dadada for less important data points.
distinctiveRules.quote: Primary color on charts. Use when only one color is required... Secondary color on charts. Use for the less important data points.

distinctiveRules.rule: Categorical series follow the numbered sequence brown #8c510a, red-orange #d73027, purple #a06fae, teal #2b8078, blue #638ec2.
distinctiveRules.quote: For data visualization only. Follow the numbered sequence.

distinctiveRules.rule: Every colour token has a light- and dark-mode value; dark-mode chart surface #2b3033, text #c3d0d9, gridlines #9aa5ae; sequential ramps invert in dark mode.
distinctiveRules.quote: #ffffff / #2b3033 chart - Surface and border on chart UI.

distinctiveRules.rule: Gridlines use the chart-border token (#8a8a8a light); only horizontal gridlines on column/line charts, no y-axis line.
Legend sits centred below the chart with small circular swatches and secondary-text colour #494a4a.
distinctiveRules.quote: chart-text-secondary: Secondary text for legends (illustrations: '● Legend 1 ● Legend 2' below the x axis)

distinctiveRules.rule: Y-axis title is rotated vertically on the left and carries the unit in parentheses.
distinctiveRules.quote: Illustration axis title 'Rainfall (mm)' rotated beside the y axis

distinctiveRules.rule: On hover, keep the focused bar segment in colour, dim/darken the others, and show a callout with a bold value and a smaller descriptor line.
Line charts must differentiate series by marker shape, dash pattern and line thickness, not colour alone.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use different shapes, lines and thicknesses on line charts.

distinctiveRules.rule: Each fill colour scheme has a matching darker 'chart-border' stroke token (e.g. brown fill with #a36e29 border).
Sequential palettes are 6 steps; diverging palettes are 3+3 steps built from two sequential schemes (e.g. orange #d73027 -> #fee090 | #e0f3f8 -> #4575b4).
distinctiveRules.quote: numbered suffixes such as 'start-1' and 'end-4' identify the specific shades

referenceImages.describes: 'Do' example (green check): horizontal bar chart, all ten bars in a single medium blue (~#116fae) with slightly rounded ends, category numbers 1-10 on the left in large grey sans, value ticks 0-300 at the bottom, no gridlines, no axis lines, no title or legend.

'Do' example for accessibility: stacked columns Jan-May, lower segment pink, upper segment light green, separated by a thin white line; very light grey horizontal gridlines at 10-unit steps, small grey tick numbers 0-50, rotated y title 'Rainfall (mm)', no axis lines, legend centred below with circle swatches 'Legend 1' (green) and 'Legend 2' (pink) in dark grey Open Sans.

'Do' hover-feedback example: same stacked column chart where the hovered April column keeps light-green/pink colours while all other columns turn dark (dark olive over dark plum); a borderless callout above shows bold '38%' and '15 tasks' beneath; cursor arrow on the hovered segment; x labels of non-hovered months bold; legend below centred with circles.

Montage of the six best-practice illustrations (do left with green check, don't right with red '!'): single-blue vs rainbow horizontal bars; pink/green vs blue/green stacked columns; hover state dimming others vs no dimming. Shows consistent chrome: light horizontal gridlines, no axis lines, rotated unit y-title, bottom-centred circle legend.
